title: Safety Stock Optimization for CPG
text: Safety stock for CPG products must account for demand variability (CV), supplier lead time variability, and target service level. Formula: SS = Z × σ_LT × D̄ where Z=1.65 for 95% service level, σ_LT is std dev of lead time demand, D̄ is average daily demand. For fast-moving items like Shampoo Pro and Detergent Powder, safety stock of 15-20 days is recommended under normal conditions, increasing to 30-45 days during identified supply risk events. Dynamic safety stock models should incorporate real-time event triggers from supply chain intelligence feeds. [Source: CPG Industry Intelligence Report Q4 2024, Confidence: 0.93]

title: Event-Triggered Demand Sensing
text: Traditional demand forecasting (ARIMA, exponential smoothing) fails to capture exogenous supply chain shocks. Modern CPG supply chain intelligence integrates event triggers: tariff announcements cause 10-30% demand spikes as retailers pre-buy; route closures cause 5-20% demand suppression due to shelf-out; war disruptions cause 25-60% demand surges for essential categories. Event trigger taxonomy: Level-1 (monitor), Level-2 (prepare alternate source), Level-3 (activate emergency procurement), Level-4 (force majeure). ML models trained on event-demand pairs achieve 15-25% better MAPE vs baseline for disruption periods. [Source: CPG Industry Intelligence Report Q3 2024, Confidence: 0.9]

title: Multi-Tier Supply Chain Visibility
text: CPG companies need visibility beyond Tier-1 suppliers. Key metrics: Tier-1 supplier risk score, Tier-2 concentration risk (>30% from single source = high risk). For a CPG portfolio of 50+ SKUs, recommended technology stack: supply chain control tower (SAP IBP, o9 Solutions, or Kinaxis), AI demand sensing layer (with event ingestion from geopolitical risk feeds), carrier performance monitoring (Flexport, project44), n-tier supplier mapping (Resilinc, riskmethods). Critical KPIs: Perfect Order Rate >95%, OTIF >92%, Forecast Accuracy >85% (WMAPE), Cash-to-Cash Cycle <45 days. [Source: CPG Industry Intelligence Report Q3 2024, Confidence: 0.93]

title: Tariff Impact Assessment Framework
text: When tariffs are announced, CPG supply chain teams must execute: (1) SKU-level cost impact analysis within 48h — map each SKU to HS codes and calculate landed cost change. (2) Alternate sourcing feasibility — identify countries with preferential trade agreements (FTA). (3) Pre-build analysis — calculate optimal inventory build quantity: Q* = min(storage_capacity, demand_forecast × coverage_days). (4) Price elasticity modeling — determine how much cost can be passed to consumer vs absorbed. (5) Hedge procurement for 6-12 months where shelf life permits. Affected categories in CPG: personal care (high chemical content = high tariff sensitivity), packaged foods (agricultural commodity input sensitivity). [Source: CPG Industry Intelligence Report Q3 2024, Confidence: 0.88]

title: Supply Chain KPI Benchmarks for CPG
text: Industry benchmarks for CPG supply chains (2024): Inventory turnover: 8-12x/year (top quartile >15x). Days inventory outstanding (DIO): 30-45 days. Order fill rate: 97%+ (top performers 99.5%).
